cards.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.33303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. cards.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. cards.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.33190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. cards.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. cards.title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.33161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an LLM or VLM produces several candidate answers, picking the best one usually relies on the model's own confidence, a learned judge model, or a domain check. Each has a known weakness: an answer can be fluent but insecure, mathematically plausible but physically infeasible, or rated highly by a judge while quietly breaking a task requirement. cards.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.33160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in chart-to-code generation. However, existing benchmarks mainly focus on static charts, overlooking interactive charts that enable richer and more expressive data exploration. cards.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. cards.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act. In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data science workflows often require tools that presume non-trivial technical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) reduce this barrier, but a gap remains between flexible general-purpose agents and statistically controlled pipelines. We introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data-agent platform that combines reusable, LLM-selected skills with deterministic diagnostic guardrails. cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis.
